thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert — Elevated 5xx and request timeouts observed across /v1/generate endpoints in us-west-2. Error rate spiking to ~18% over last 2m; automated detection flagged queue depth increase on scheduler pools. Paging oncall now. @oncall_alex :rotating_light:

oncall_alex: I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking dashboards. initial hypothesis: batching/scheduler saturation causing head-of-line blocking.

sre_jordan: I see LOTS of inflight batches stuck at the scheduler level. KV cache size normal but batch formation times are > 900ms for many requests. Gateway is timing out at 10s -> cascading 504s.

runtime_maya: can you paste the scheduler stats? I want batch sizes, flush latency, and backlog per queue.

sre_jordan: paste: ```
SCHED_POOL: default
- queue_depth: 4200
- avg_batch_size: 18
- avg_flush_latency_ms: 1200
- longest_wait_ms: 8600
- inflight_batches: 72
- eviction_events_last_5m: 3
```

prod_support_sam: Customer impact: multiple customers reporting timeouts and degraded RLHF job runs. PS is fielding high-severity tickets; we're seeing 20% of production tokens failing on generation routes.

customer_success_lee: Notified top 5 enterprise customers about degraded performance, collecting samples. No full data loss, but elevated latencies and 5xx.

oncall_alex: Initial mitigation plan: 1) enable temporary routing fallback to smaller model class (reduces batch pressure), 2) reduce max batch wait to 200ms for us-west-2 scheduler, 3) enable aggressive KV cache prefix routing to bypass hot queues, 4) if not improved in 5m, trigger scheduler recycle. Implementing 1 and 2 now.

deploy-bot: /route update applied: traffic split 80% -> fallback-small-model, 20% -> primary. /config update applied: scheduler.max_batch_wait_ms=200 for pool=us-west-2-default.

runtime_maya: live metrics after config change: ```
- queue_depth: 3100 (down)
- avg_flush_latency_ms: 480
- avg_batch_size: 12
- inflight_batches: 44
- 5xx_rate: 9% -> trending down
```

prod_support_sam: seeing fewer new tickets but some long-tail failures for heavy context jobs. Customers with long sequence lengths still hitting timeouts.

sre_jordan: root cause notes: sudden traffic pattern with bursty long-context requests caused batching windows to hold many requests waiting for token alignment -> head-of-line blocking. Combined with a small number of slow model-serving tasks (likely GC or kernel stall) exacerbated queues. Need to isolate slow-serving hosts.

oncall_alex: I'm kicking off a host-level diagnostic to find slow nodes. @runtime_maya can you tag and evict hosts with >95th percentile latency? Evicting rather than restart to avoid warmup.

runtime_maya: running: ```
/infra/tools/evict --pool us-west-2-default --latency-gt 1200ms --dry-run=false
```

eng_manager_ravi: Heads up — if we need to recycle the scheduler, coordinate with SRE for a staged drain to avoid global loss. Prioritize minimal customer impact.

oncall_alex: Eviction started. Rolling out evictions on 6 hosts flagged as slow. Also increasing batch eviction aggressiveness to preempt long-wait batches.

runtime_maya: Post-eviction snapshot: ```
- queue_depth: 900
- avg_flush_latency_ms: 220
- avg_batch_size: 10
- inflight_batches: 18
- 5xx_rate: 2.8%
- timeouts: down to baseline+1.2%
```

prod_support_sam: CS reports improved response times for most customers. One enterprise still seeing intermittent failures for >32k token jobs; recommended workaround: split requests or route to dedicated capacity.

customer_success_lee: Notifying affected enterprise about mitigation and recommended workaround. Offering to migrate heavy job traffic to dedicated queue if needed.

sre_jordan: Root cause summary to capture: traffic spike of long-context requests + a few nodes with anomalous model-serving stalls -> head-of-line blocking in scheduler -> increased batch wait -> gateway timeouts and 5xx. Contributing factors: conservative batch wait defaults, insufficient proactive slow-host eviction.

oncall_alex: Actions completed: fallback routing applied, max_batch_wait decreased, slow hosts evicted, batch eviction policy tightened. Next actions: 1) post-incident follow-up to tune batch wait heuristics per workload, 2) add alert for long_wait_ms > 2s per pool, 3) consider per-tenant dedicated lanes for high-context jobs.

eng_manager_ravi: Agreed. Please prepare a short incident blameless summary for the morning postmortem and include customer impact metrics + timeline. Assigning follow-ups: SRE to add alert, Runtime to create per-tenant lane design doc, Product to evaluate dedicated capacity offers for the affected customers.

oncall_alex: Handing off to daytime oncall @sre_jordan for follow-up. I'll be offline for the next 2h but reachable for questions. :white_check_mark:

sre_jordan: Taking over. I'll draft timeline and collect traces/logs.

incident-bot: Incident updated to SEV2 -> mitigated. Notes: fallback routing + host eviction reduced error rate from ~18% -> ~3%. Postmortem required if customer impact > 5 customers or services degraded >30m.

prod_support_sam: Logging root-cause notes in ops-runbook and flagging top impacted customers for outreach.

customer_success_lee: Sent tailored note to affected enterprise partners with status and mitigation steps.

oncall_alex: Thanks team — great quick coordination. Closing live-handoff.
